newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Petrobras BR eyes natgas market.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Petrobras BR eyes natgas market.

text.p: Brazilian state oil products distributor Petrobras BR Distribuidora, a unit of federal oil monopoly Petrobras, wants to expand in Brazil's promising natgas market, a senior company official said.

BR Finance and Market Relations Director Reynaldo Aloy said the company was planning to invest $20 million to $40 million in the natgas sector this year out of total 1997 investments of $180 million to $200 million.

"Gas is an important issue in the company," Aloy said. "We want to sell as much gas as possible. It is a clean energy source and only two percent of Brazilian energy use is gas. But by the year 2005 the government wants gas to represent 10 percent of energy use."
He said the company was interested in gaining shares in Sao Paulo state gas company Comgas and Minas Gerais state gas firm Gasmig, both up for privatization this year.
"We haven't defined yet how we would like to participate in these companies," he said. "We are waiting for an opportunity."
BR already has stakes in 12 state gas companies across Brazil and owns 15 outlets for industrial use gas to which it wants to add another eight this year.
Shell Brasil SA, a unit of Royal Dutch Shell, paid 74 million reais ($69.8 million) for a 20-percent stake in Comgas in October also with the intention of expanding in the Brazilian gas market.
((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151))
